$note: Written after rendering the reel and looking at full-resolution stills from it — not from the contact sheet, which is an overview and not an inspection. Scores are one person's judgement out of ten and are deliberately NOT computed: every reel this repo has shipped broken passed the computed gates.
question: How Did Humans Move Stones Weighing Over 1,000 Tons?
verdict: The load is now a mass rather than an outline: limestone with a body value under the raking light, a contact shadow where it meets the sledge, and speckle you can see. It is also the RIGHT size for the first time — three men tall and most of the frame wide, derived from the figure beside it instead of chosen — and it is the SAME load in all fourteen shots, sized once from the reel's largest stated figure. It travels the way the men are pulling, which it did not before: the rope, the arrow and the position now agree. Ground and sky read as surfaces, so the band of drawing is standing in a space rather than floating in a black rectangle.
whatWorked: Scale is measured against the load itself, in man-heights ticked off its face, which asserts nothing.
Rollers turn at the speed the load moves and the rope pulls its own slack out and settles.
Registration ticks and the disclosure plate stay pinned while the camera moves, so nothing is sliced off the frame edge.
Fourteen shots of one object, and it is recognisably one object.
whatFailed: The frame is still mostly air and floor: a five-to-one beam in 9:16 leaves a band, and the vertical space carries type or nothing.
Three lines are still typography with no picture behind them.

remainingDefects.what: No photograph anywhere in the reel
One drawing kind carries fourteen of twenty shots
remainingDefects.why: variety comes from camera and stage, not from a second kind
